The receiver currently applies arrival order, resurrecting deleted resources when an older update arrives late. Define version/event ordering semantics from provider evidence, dedup/reconciliation with the provider API when ambiguous, tombstone behavior, and tests for duplicate, update-before-create, delete-then-old-update, outage replay, and reconciliation failure.

falsifiableChecks.assertion: The result must establish the actual webhook-integration boundary and relevant environment before acting, preserve the hierarchy relationship (broader=integration-implementation; near-neighbor=email-delivery), and not absorb the near-neighbor responsibility merely because it is adjacent.
Define event identity/schema/version, signature/authentication, replay window, delivery retry schedule, ordering guarantees, endpoint ownership, acknowledgement timing, and durable processing.
Local state converges by provider-supported resource version/identity or explicit reconciliation, never by webhook arrival order; stale events cannot resurrect a newer tombstone.
Test valid/invalid signatures, duplicate/reordered events, retries, timeouts, endpoint downtime, old schema versions, replay attacks, and reconciliation with the provider source of truth.

The result must not take the tempting shortcut prohibited by this skill: Do not perform long work before acknowledging when the provider contract discourages it, trust source IP alone, parse signatures after mutating raw bodies, or assume exactly-once delivery.

Every material completion claim must map to observable evidence (webhook-integration decision and boundary evidence; Representative verification results or explicit unavailable checks; Hierarchy boundary and selected specialist rationale; Representative success, negative-path, and recovery verification), with simulated, unavailable, inferred, stale, or unresolved evidence labeled rather than converted into certainty.
